Both containing-envelope candidates have explicit nonnegative John weights satisfying the first and identity second moments, proving unrestricted optimality. Endpoint algebra and positive-definite spectra are checked. Python exact rationals passed 9,900 parameter profiles, 504,900 cardinality comparisons, and 69,394 masks; finite tests are not the infinity proof.

originality.rationale: The existing capped-cube John theorem computes the ellipsoid of a strictly larger envelope, so it alone does not imply this theorem for a partial permutohedron; the necessary uniform missing-subset feasibility/screening theorem is established here. Earlier partial-permutohedron results concern facets, scalar inballs and enclosing Löwner ellipsoids rather than maximal-volume inscribed ellipsoids. The new theorem is an exact classification over all two integer parameters, with a rigorously proved complete contact law. Possible coverage under other polymatroid language is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent older general theorem on John ellipsoids of symmetric polymatroids or optimal designs could imply the subset-screening statement; targeted searches cannot prove absence.
Other non-indexed sources or differently named subset-sum polytope families may contain the statement.

value.rationale: The full-dimensional family P(m,n) has potentially exponentially many subset facets. The theorem gives its complete John ellipsoid in closed form for every pair (m,n), including an anisotropic transition and precise contacts, by proving a genuinely nontrivial all-facet screening result. This determines a canonical geometric invariant for natural partial permutation polytopes and explains how apparently complex facet structure becomes invisible to maximum-volume ellipsoids, rather than merely recomputing a known capped-cube formula.
